item.statement: Achieving a simultaneous balance of high strength and high ductility in single-phased high-entropy alloys remains an unsolved challenge.
quotes: Basically, single-phased HEAs have been found difficult to reach a reasonable balance between strength and (tensile) ductility
Single-phased fcc structured HEAs are ductile but not strong enough
Single-phased bcc structured HEAs, on the other hand, can be very strong but at the price of brittleness

item.statement: No high-entropy alloy has previously been reported to possess an excellent balanced combination of strength and tensile ductility.
quotes: To the best of our knowledge, there is no report of HEAs possessing an excellent balanced strength and tensile ductility
A simultaneous achievement of both still constitutes a tough challenge
The inferior castability and compositional segregation of HEAs are also obstacles for their technological applications

item.statement: Simply combining fcc and bcc phases without a specific structural design failed to solve the strength-ductility balance problem.
item.system: Composite HEAs with random fcc/bcc mixtures
quotes: However, simply introducing a combination of fcc and bcc phases, without a proper structural design, could not solve the problem
Moreover, the inferior castability and compositional segregation, which are common for HEAs, further downgrade their mechanical properties
To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept

item.statement: Conventional NiAl-based alloys suffer from a tradeoff between low ductility at room temperature and low strength at high temperatures.
item.lever: Composition (creating pseudo-binary NiAl/(Co, Cr, Fe) system)
quotes: The major disadvantages for NiAl are the low ductility at room temperature and the low strength at high-temperatures
which also constitute the motivation to develop NiAl/Cr(Mo) eutectic alloys
compared to NiAl or NiAl/Cr(Mo) eutectic alloys, the EHEA exhibited a much higher fracture strength, and more importantly, a simultaneously much higher ductility at room temperature

item.statement: Conventional high-performance alloys like Ni-based superalloys have high strength but suffer from high density compared to the new EHEA.
quotes: It is stressed here that the density of this EHEA was measured to be 7.38 g/cm 3 , much lower than those of Ni-based superalloys typically with a density of above 8.0 g/cm 3

Further optimization of the room-temperature and elevated temperature properties while maintaining this relatively lower density, will certainly enable EHEAs to become competitive high-temperature alloys to Ni-based superalloys
The EHEA exhibited a much higher fracture strength, and more importantly, a simultaneously much higher ductility at room temperature

quotes: We choose to not to call it the yield stress, as the mechanism for such a low elastic limit is still unclear at this stage
